title: Surjectivity on first Tor after a flat intermediate base change
statement: Let $R\to A\to B$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings and $M$ an $R$-module. Assume $M\otimes_RA$ is a flat $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then the natural $B$-linear map $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,A)\otimes_AB\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,B)$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], induced by $A\to B$ in the second variable, is surjective.

proof.text: Compute Tor using the chosen projective resolution P of M and its tensor complexes KA and KB. Lift the given Tor element to a cycle of KB using the epimorphism homologyπ, after transporting through P.isoLeftDerivedObj. The augmentation P₁ → P₀ → M is exact and its final arrow is surjective.

Apply tensor_cycles_flat_cokernel to that exact augmented presentation and the flatness hypothesis. Express the degree-one cycle over B as a finite sum of coefficient images of degree-one cycles over A, each multiplied by its specified coefficient bᵢ.

Regard each lifted cycle xᵢ as an element cᵢ of KA.cycles using moduleCatCyclesIso.inv. Naturality of iCycles and its injectivity identify the original KB cycle with the sum of cyclesMap(φᵢ)(cᵢ), where φᵢ is the tensor chain map induced by coefficient multiplication composed with A → B. Take aᵢ = isoLeftDerivedObj.inv(homologyπ(cᵢ)). The tensor sum Σ aᵢ ⊗ bᵢ maps to the prescribed Tor element: torOneBaseChange_tmul, functoriality, ProjectiveResolution.leftDerived_app_eq, the inverse identities of the resolution comparison isomorphisms, and homologyπ_naturality give the equality term by term. This proves surjectivity without any new unproved statement.
